title: Icon
description: One icon of the set: inline SVG by default, or a canvas drawn with WebGPU, WebGL2, WebGL or Canvas2D. Named components (SearchIcon…), the generic Icon, custom icons and icons chosen by name.

intro.title: SVG or canvas
intro.svg: By default an icon is an inline <svg>: it renders on the server, follows the text color through currentColor and the font size with size="1em", and is hidden from assistive technologies unless it has a title or an aria-label.
intro.canvas: With renderer set to "auto", "webgpu", "webgl2", "webgl" or "canvas2d", the same icon is drawn on a canvas. Browsers cap live WebGL contexts at about 16, so canvas icons share one backend per page: the icons that changed are packed into an atlas, drawn in one pass and copied to their canvases. "auto" follows the global default (setDefaultIconRenderer), here the renderer bar.
intro.bundle: Only what you import is bundled: SearchIcon brings its own path data, the canvas renderers load with the first canvas icon, and DynamicIcon (names chosen at runtime) is the only component that bundles the whole set.

basic.title: Basic
basic.description: Every icon is a component named after it; icons sit inline with text and inside buttons.

size-color.title: Size and color
size-color.description: size takes pixels or any CSS length (1em follows the font size); color takes any CSS color, theme variables included, and defaults to the text color.

stroke.title: Stroke width
stroke.description: strokeWidth is on the 24×24 grid, so it scales with the icon. absoluteStrokeWidth keeps it in pixels whatever the size (second half of the bottom row).

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.description: Decorative icons are aria-hidden; give an icon that stands alone a title (role="img"); inside a control, label the control instead.

custom.title: Custom icons
custom.description: defineIcon validates your own path data once; createIcon turns it into a component like the built-in ones, and Icon draws it on every renderer.

dynamic.title: Icons by name
dynamic.description: DynamicIcon picks a built-in icon from a name known only at runtime; unknown names render nothing. It bundles the whole set.

canvas.title: Renderers
canvas.description: The same icon as SVG and on each canvas backend; under each one, the backend that actually drew it. "auto" follows the renderer bar; a forced backend this browser lacks falls back to the next one.

IconProps.icon: The icon to draw: a built-in one (e.g. searchIcon) or a defineIcon result
IconProps.size: Width and height; a number is in pixels, canvas renderers also follow CSS sizes such as "1em"
IconProps.strokeWidth: Stroke width on the 24×24 grid (scales with the size)
IconProps.absoluteStrokeWidth: Keeps strokeWidth in pixels whatever the size
IconProps.title: Accessible name: the icon becomes role="img"; without it (or an aria-label) the icon is hidden from assistive technologies
IconProps.renderer: Inline SVG, or a canvas drawn by a backend shared by every canvas icon of the page ("auto" follows the global default)
IconProps.onRendererChange: Canvas renderers: called with the backend that drew the icon
IconProps.ref: The <svg> element, or the <canvas> with a canvas renderer

DynamicIconProps.name: Name of a built-in icon (e.g. "arrow-up"); unknown names render nothing

props.label: Accessible name: the icon becomes role="img" with this name; without it, the icon is hidden from assistive technologies

events.minerva-renderer-change: Canvas mode: the backend drew the icon, or fell back after a GPU loss; detail: { renderer }

methods.getRenderer: Backend drawing the canvas (webgpu, webgl2, webgl, canvas2d), null in SVG mode or until it started

basic.title: Basic
basic.description: <minerva-icon> draws a built-in icon by name, inline with text and in the slots of other elements; with a label it becomes an image for assistive technologies.

canvas.title: Renderers
canvas.description: The renderer attribute draws the icon on a canvas; each icon fires minerva-renderer-change with the backend that drew it, shown under it. "auto" follows the renderer bar; a forced backend this browser lacks falls back to the next one.
